claims.text: Direct elemental Cr coatings on zirconium-alloy substrates undergo elevated-temperature Cr–Zr interdiffusion that causes premature coating failure.
The proposed intervention is a few-nanometer Al-rich interlayer between the zirconium-alloy substrate and the elemental Cr coating.
The Al-rich interlayer will inhibit elevated-temperature Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
Inhibiting Cr–Zr interdiffusion will prevent premature coating failure during accident-relevant high-temperature steam exposure.
The interlayer-modified Cr coating will maintain protection during normal subcritical-water operation.
Normal-operation conditions are approximately 300–400°C in subcritical water for extended periods.
The relevant accident condition is approximately 1200°C steam exposure for periods on the order of minutes.
The Al-rich interlayer will form a stable, continuous Al2O3 layer at the Cr/Al interface.
During high-temperature steam exposure, Al in the buried interlayer will oxidize preferentially to form dense, adherent Al2O3.
The Al2O3 layer will act as a diffusion barrier that restricts atomic interdiffusion between Cr and Zr.
Restricting Cr–Zr interdiffusion will preserve the integrity of the Cr coating.
The proposed barrier will remain stable under normal subcritical-water conditions and will not impair overall protective performance.
Relative to an unmodified Cr coating, the interlayer-modified coating will show significantly less Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
Reduced interdiffusion will produce enhanced coating integrity and sustained accident tolerance during transient high-temperature steam events.
Performance during substantially longer or hotter exposures is uncertain.
The optimal interlayer thickness and Al concentration require optimization to avoid compromising adhesion and cyclic thermal performance.
A controlled comparison at 1200°C for 5 minutes can test the effect of the Al-rich interlayer against an otherwise identical direct-Cr baseline.

The hypothesis is falsified if the interlayer fails to produce a statistically significant reduction in Cr–Zr interdiffusion, fails to form stable Al2O3, or compromises adhesion relative to the baseline.
